description.summary: An aggressive tree-dwelling creature that hurls dead branches and wood at lumberjacks from the forest canopy, more violent than its cousin the Agropelter.
description.full: The Argopelter is a variant or cousin of the Agropelter, distinguished by its more aggressive and targeted attacks on lumberjacks. Living in the forest canopy, this creature specifically targets workers with barrages of dead branches, limbs, and chunks of wood. Unlike the Agropelter which throws at any passerby, the Argopelter has particular hatred for lumberjacks and loggers, perhaps in retaliation for cutting down its forest home. The creature is rarely if ever seen, known only by the sudden assault of falling wood that seems too directed to be accidental. Like many fearsome critters, it provided a humorous explanation for the genuine hazard of widow-makers (falling dead branches).

etymology.meaning: Variant spelling of Agropelter; 'pelter' meaning one who pelts/throws

related_phenomena.name: Agropelter
related_phenomena.description: Less aggressive variant that throws wood at any passerby

abilities.description: Hurls dead branches and wood with force and accuracy at lumberjacks
Specifically aims at lumberjacks rather than random passersby

patterns: Motivated by apparent revenge for tree-cutting

origins.cultural_roots: American occupational folklore from lumber camps
origins.folklore_connections: Variant of Agropelter with added motivation (revenge against loggers)

folklore.beliefs: Explained widow-maker hazard as revenge from forest-dwelling creature; added element of forest fighting back against logging

literature: Fearsome Creatures of the Lumberwoods by William T. Cox (1910)
